commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Detect unloaded NVFP4 weight scales with a NaN sentinel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fail during loading when a ModelOpt NVFP4 linear layer's `weight_scale` was not fully populated, instead of producing NaN outputs later. This can happen when a mixed-precision checkpoint stores the layer as BF16 but the layer is not excluded from NVFP4 quantization.

Initialize per-block `weight_scale` values to NaN, then check for remaining NaNs in `KNvfp4Static.process()` after casting to FP32 for backend compatibility. If any remain, raise a `RuntimeError` identifying the layer and suggesting that it be excluded from quantization. This detects skipped or partial scale loading without relying on the contents of `torch.empty()` memory.

This complements #45320, which checks missing per-expert scales in the MoE path. This PR covers per-block scales in the linear path. #42601 addresses activation-scale clamping for dead experts, a separate NaN source.

## Validation

- Current rebase: `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual --show-diff-on-failure` — all hooks passed, including Ruff, clang-format, and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13.
- `git range-diff` confirms all three reviewed patches are unchanged by the rebase onto `6fbb00b18`.
- Previously validated the NaN-sentinel check on GB10/CUDA with completely unloaded and partially loaded scales; casting to FP32 preserved detection in both cases.
- The original guard was validated while serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 2× DGX Spark (GB10), TP=2: the affected checkpoint failed during startup with the offending layer identified, while a fully FP4 checkpoint loaded successfully.
- The GB10/model checks were not rerun for this rebase.

The rebase includes upstream #55630, which fixes the unrelated CUDA comment formatting that failed the previous pre-commit run.

AI assistance was used to prepare and rebase this PR. The hardware and model validation above was previously reported by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Test][Determinism] Cover VLM batch invariance in default execution mode
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

- add a focused Qwen3-VL batch-invariance case for the default (non-eager) execution mode
- keep the existing eager image/video coverage while sharing the common runner
- fail closed when selected-token logprobs or the expected number of outputs/tokens are missing
- disable prefix/MM processor caches and the FlashInfer sampler so the test isolates the intended execution-mode comparison

## Why this is not duplicate work

#53531 added the current VLM batch-invariance test, but all of its cases set `enforce_eager=True`. This PR adds one deliberately narrow default-execution cell, which exercises CUDA Graph decode without multiplying the full image/video × encoder-backend matrix.

I checked #27433 and searched open PRs for the issue number and for `VLM batch invariance default execution`; no open PR covered this scope when this PR was created. The maintainer also invited investigation of non-eager mode in #27433.

## Validation

Environment: RTX 4090 (SM89), BF16, TP=1, vLLM `7de70fa7ae9fdda688257eed13639b56cc677fde`, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct at revision `89644892e4d85e24eaac8bacfd4f463576704203`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance_vlm.py::test_vlm_batch_invariance_default_execution \
  -v
# 1 passed, 15 warnings in 35.80s

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  'tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance_vlm.py::test_vlm_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN[FLASH_ATTN-image]' \
  -v
# 1 passed, 15 warnings in 20.03s

git diff --check
# passed
```

An instrumented validation run, removed before the tests above, confirmed that all seven target decode steps in the four-request default-execution run used FULL CUDA Graph replay with at least three logically active requests per step. All four images were actually encoder-computed. Solo versus batched runs had identical generated token IDs and identical FP32 bit patterns for each selected token's logprob; maximum absolute logprob difference was 0.

The target prefill and vision encoder remained eager, so this result is intentionally limited to default-execution/CUDA-Graph decode coverage. It does not claim prefill or encoder graph coverage. This is a test-only change and does not alter model output or serving behavior, so no model-quality evaluation is applicable.

### Blackwell follow-up

Per review feedback, I repeated the two target tests on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (SM120, 32 GB), driver 595.71.05, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.13. The vLLM commit and fixed model revision were unchanged from the RTX 4090 run above.


The longer default-execution time included first-use Triton/`ptxas-blackwell` compilation for SM120.

commits.pr_title: [Pooling] Report actual input token usage for scoring APIs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`/score` and `/rerank` calculated usage from post-processed `PoolingRequestOutput.prompt_token_ids`. For bi-encoder and late-interaction models, post-processing repeats a shared query for every document and inserts a synthetic separator token. Those implementation details inflated reported token usage for 1:N requests even though the engine encoded the query only once.

This PR calculates usage from the rendered engine inputs that were actually submitted. It fixes bi-encoder and late-interaction accounting while preserving cross-encoder accounting, scores, request processing, and output ordering.

## Reproducer

Start an MRV2 pooling server:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  intfloat/multilingual-e5-small \
  --runner pooling \
  --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \
  --port 8127
```

In another shell, compare tokenizer-derived input length with both scoring APIs:

```bash
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import requests

base = "http://127.0.0.1:8127"
model = "intfloat/multilingual-e5-small"
query = "alpha beta"
documents = ["gamma", "delta epsilon", "zeta eta theta"]

counts = []
for text in [query, *documents]:
    response = requests.post(
        f"{base}/tokenize",
        json={"model": model, "prompt": text, "add_special_tokens": True},
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    counts.append(response.json()["count"])

print("token_counts", counts, "actual_sum", sum(counts))
for endpoint in ["/rerank", "/score"]:
    payload = (
        {"model": model, "query": query, "documents": documents}
        if endpoint == "/rerank"
        else {"model": model, "queries": query, "documents": documents}
    )
    response = requests.post(f"{base}{endpoint}", json=payload)
    response.raise_for_status()
    print(endpoint, response.json()["usage"])
PY
```

## Output on `main`

```text
token_counts [5, 3, 6, 7] actual_sum 21
/rerank {'prompt_tokens': 34, 'total_tokens': 34}
/score {'prompt_tokens': 34, 'total_tokens': 34, 'completion_tokens': 0, 'prompt_tokens_details': None, 'completion_tokens_details': None}
```

The 13-token excess is deterministic for three documents:
`(3 - 1) * 5 query tokens + 3 synthetic separator tokens`.

## Output on this branch

```text
token_counts [5, 3, 6, 7] actual_sum 21
/rerank {'prompt_tokens': 21, 'total_tokens': 21}
/score {'prompt_tokens': 21, 'total_tokens': 21, 'completion_tokens': 0, 'prompt_tokens_details': None, 'completion_tokens_details': None}
```

```bash
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_late_interaction_serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_utils.py -q
# 17 passed, 14 warnings in 2.13s

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<H100_GPU_INDEX> \

  tests/models/language/pooling/test_max_tokens_per_doc.py -q
# 20 passed, 15 warnings in 195.44s

```

Additional MRV2 end-to-end checks:

- `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`: `/rerank` and `/score` both changed from 34 to the tokenizer-derived total of 21; scores were unchanged.
- `answerdotai/answerai-colbert-small-v1`: flash and vanilla late-interaction  paths both reported 16 input tokens instead of 27; scores matched to FP16  precision.
- `cross-encoder/ms-marco-TinyBERT-L2-v2`: usage remained 21, matching the sum of the three paired inputs.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Fix ValueError on KV load failure with a hybrid KV cache
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
`_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` unpacks `get_block_ids()` -- which
returns one block-id list per KV cache group -- into a single name:

    # TODO (davidb): add support for hybrid memory allocator
    (req_block_ids,) = self.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)

so the first reported invalid block on a hybrid (Mamba/SSM plus attention)
model raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)` inside the
scheduler. Nothing catches it, so EngineCore calls `_send_engine_dead()` and
exits: one recoverable read failure takes down every request on the instance,
not just the one that failed.

A hybrid model's groups sit on different block grids, so the same block index
means a different token position in each and there is no single longest valid
prefix to truncate at. Rather than build a block-level answer for that -- per-
block error handling is being removed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42461 -- affected hybrid requests
recompute in full, which is the granularity that replacement moves to anyway.
Single-group models keep the existing block-level truncation untouched.

Blocks are still added to `marked_invalid_block_ids` so a request sharing one
of them is rescheduled as before.

The null block needs excluding on this path. In Mamba `align` mode a group's
block list is mostly the shared null block -- a 9-chunk request looks like
`[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 10]`, only the aligned snapshot is backed -- so
without the guard a reported null block would restart unrelated requests, and
`blocks_to_evict` would collect a block that belongs to no request.

And also: `pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py`

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EPD] Preserve explicit multimodal UUIDs with caches disabled
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Preserve explicit multimodal UUIDs when both prefix caching and processor caching are disabled. Only missing UUIDs receive request-local IDs; other hashing behavior is unchanged.

Currently, disabling both caches replaces even proxy-provided UUIDs with frontend-local IDs, so E and consumer can use different identifiers for the same image. An ECExample cache miss or NIXL announcement lookup miss can then fall through to local encoding. Since the rewritten request contains only metadata, not image tensors, this triggers `Expected multimodal embeddings ... got <class 'NoneType'>` and crashes the consumer engine. Mooncake instead waits for the mismatched identifier and times out.

Unlike #55583, #55616 and #36692, this fixes UUID replacement with both caches disabled, not media-cache lookup or cache-key configuration.

commits.pr_title: [DS V4.1][Engram] Support async prefetch for offloaded engram lookups and engram DP sharding
commits.pr_body:
Re-open of #56357, rebased onto `main`. The original PR was stacked on
the `dsv41-feat` staging branch and was auto-closed when that branch was
removed after DeepSeek V4.1 merged to main. It now targets `main`
directly and also carries the engram DP-shard support commit that was
previously split out as #56230 (also auto-closed for the same reason).

## What's New

Three commits: engram DP sharding (from #56230) plus two engram
embedding I/O improvements for DeepSeek V4.1:

**0. DP sharding for engram tables (previously #56230).** Engram tables
are sharded across a node-local engram DP (EDP) group instead of being
fully replicated per DP rank; per-step all_gathers trade tokens for
heads so each rank can serve its local shard. Set
`--engram-config.enable_engram_dp_sharding false` to retain TP-only tables
(default: true). This is independent of `embedding_across_dp`; explicitly
enabled DP shared memory still uses a node-local group. Qwen4Exp keeps using
its existing ETP group and does not create an extra EDP group. Row-wise
sharding for configurations with too few hash heads remains a TODO.

**1. Asynchronous lookup prefetch (cpu_offload path).** With
`cpu_offload`, engram table rows live in pinned host memory and are read
over UVA. The lookup used to run inline on the main stream when each
engram layer executes; `prepare_embeddings()` now starts it on a
per-layer side stream at forward entry — the n-gram hash ids for all
engram layers are known before the decoder layers run — with a halved
grid to leave SMs for the main stream. `embed()` only waits on the
stream. `@eager_break_during_capture` keeps the side-stream work out of
captured graphs, and persistent per-layer staging buffers keep
addresses stable across replays. DBO and microbatching are not supported
with DeepSeek V4.1 Engram and are rejected during configuration validation.

**2. Shared host tables (`EngramConfig.enable_engram_dp_shared_memory`,
requires `cpu_offload`).** Engram hashes are deterministic and
replica-independent (tokenizer-derived token map, layer-seeded
multipliers), so DP replicas on one node can share one physical copy of
each TP slice instead of pinning private shards and trading tokens for
heads with two per-step all_gathers. edp rank 0 creates a /dev/shm
backing file; every replica maps it `MAP_SHARED` and
`cudaHostRegister`s the pages; lookups read the shared pages over UVA
with no kernel changes. Only edp rank 0 writes weights (single-writer
barrier per parameter; load formats auto/safetensors/pt, including
multithreaded safetensors loading). `DPSharedEngramStorage` owns the shared
allocation, leader-only loading, and cached UVA views. It rejects replaced
parameter storage and unregisters the pages when their owner is released.
The leader broadcasts file-creation errors; ranks exchange mapping/registration
errors before unlinking, report the failing EDP rank and stage, and roll back
allocations on failure. Shared mode skips both
DP all_gathers, slot padding, and the rows-select kernel while keeping
per-rank and per-node host-link read bytes identical to the DP-shard
path; TP sharding/all_gather are unchanged.

Configuration validation requires CPU offload, DP > 1, elastic EP disabled,
and load format auto/safetensors/pt. Runtime validation checks that a node-local
Engram DP group actually formed. Group eligibility reuses the resolved Engram
configuration; the DP shard-size helper only handles node topology. Shared IPC and sufficient /dev/shm capacity
are also required.

Hashing, TP lookup, and gating remain in `common/engram.py`. The current
DP sharding, CUDA host registration, and prefetch implementation lives in
`nvidia/engram.py`; the AMD model continues to use the common resident path.

## Why not a duplicate

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "engram"` —
no open PR covers this; the only related ones (#56435, #56436, #56440)
touch SP all-to-all / lookup overlap / microbatch positions, not DP
sharding, prefetch, or shared host tables. This PR supersedes the
auto-closed #56230 and #56357 (same author). Shared host tables remain opt-in. Qwen4Exp and DeepSeek V4.1 now default
to CPU offload through `--engram-config.cpu_offload`; setting it to `false`
keeps tables on the GPU. The legacy offload environment setting is removed.

## Benchmarks

Real DeepSeek V4.1, 4xGB200, TP4, 512 output tokens, sync lookup vs
prefetch, 2 rounds each (ms):

| input / concurrency | TTFT sync → prefetch | Δ | decode/tok sync → prefetch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 / 1    | 44.66 → 45.11     | ~0     | 7.452 → 7.451 |
| 4096 / 1   | 168.16 → 167.38   | ~0     | 7.461 → 7.463 |
| 4096 / 8   | 680.98 → 677.45   | -0.52% | 13.006 → 12.969 |
| 8192 / 1   | 304.97 → 303.72   | -0.41% | 7.491 → 7.486 |
| 8192 / 8   | 1447.05 → 1440.92 | -0.42% | 10.703 → 10.683 |
| 16384 / 1  | 573.26 → 568.04   | -0.91% | 7.511 → 7.500 |
| 16384 / 8  | 2636.92 → 2613.28 | -0.90% | 11.849 → 11.882 |


Prefetch recovers exactly the lookup-bytes / host-link time on the
critical path, and is neutral in decode where lookups are us-scale — no
regression anywhere.

## Tests

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -v`
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -v --timeout=180`
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -k engram -v`
- `.venv/bin/python -O -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -k 'engram_dp_shared_memory or engram_rejects_elastic_cross_dp' -v --timeout=60`
- Pre-commit hooks on all changed files

All passed.

The model evals below predate the latest loader, topology, backend, EDP
configuration, and initialization updates. The common resident path was tested
on GB200; ROCm hardware validation has not been run.


Eval (GSM8K, DeepSeek V4.1, two runs each):
| config | accuracy |
|---|---|
| TP1xDP4 + `enable_engram_dp_shared_memory` (zero DP comm) | 0.9318 / 0.9318 |
| TP4xDP1, prefetch (default) | 0.9363 / 0.9363 |

Cross-node (official V4.1-Flash, 2 nodes, TP1xDP8 — DP spans both nodes,
so this also validates the cross-node topology for both modes):

| mode | engram group | table storage | per-step DP comm | GSM8K flex / strict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP shard | per-node Engram EDP=4 | 8 × 23.60 GiB = 188.8 GiB | yes (gather + token/head exchange) | 0.9265 / 0.9272 |
| shm | per-node Engram EDP=4 | 2 × 94.42 GiB = 188.8 GiB (each mmap'd 4×) | none | 0.9257 / 0.9257 |

Both modes work cross-node. The EDP group is a separate process group
created only for the engram tables — the general DP group is untouched
and still spans all 8 ranks across both nodes for everything else. EDP is
built from node-local DP replicas only (`_engram_dp_shard_size` =
gcd(dp_size, ranks_per_node / replica_size)), so this TP1xDP8 run forms
two independent EDP groups of 4, one per node, each sharing one full
table copy; cross-node replicas therefore see zero engram communication,
and table storage scales with node count, not replica count. The two
modes differ only intra-node: DP shard pays two all_gathers per step in
the node's EDP group, while shm eliminates them via the /dev/shm mmap.

---

AI assistance was used (Kimi Code and Codex) for rebasing, Engram changes,
and test validation. The latest Codex edits await human review.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Keep image kwargs out of video preprocessing
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Gemma4 processes video frames through the HF image processor, but currently forwards image-only overrides to that call. For example, a mixed image/video request with:

```python
mm_processor_kwargs={"images_kwargs": {"max_soft_tokens": 560}}
```

fails because the video path also passes `max_soft_tokens=70` as a top-level argument:

```text
ValueError: Keyword argument max_soft_tokens was passed two times:
in a dictionary for images_kwargs and as a **kwarg.
```

The same parameter leak can make cached and freshly processed video tensors differ. After #54918, video cache keys correctly exclude `images_kwargs`, but Gemma4 still lets options such as `images_kwargs.rescale_factor` change the video pixels. Changing an image-only option can therefore reuse video data that differs from a fresh result.

This patch clears `images_kwargs` for the video-frame call. The explicit empty override also prevents configured image options from being merged back in. Image inputs continue to receive their overrides, and videos keep the existing per-frame token budget.

Related work: #54527 fixes modality-specific parameter reads in other models, and #53610 refactors processor input handling; neither isolates Gemma4's video-frame kwargs. This also differs from #50788, which requests a configurable video token budget. The duplicate-argument error predates #54918; the cache inconsistency is an interaction with its hash scoping.

## Test Plan

The new regression test uses a mixed image/video input and covers request and configured kwargs, with and without a video UUID. It checks that image overrides still affect images, leave video tensors unchanged, and produce the same video result with a warm or cleared cache.

The test can be run with the official processor assets using:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py \
  -k video_cache_is_independent_of_image_kwargs -q
```

## Test Result

Local CPU validation on `e52be1a62d`, using Transformers 5.16.1:

- Before the fix: all 8 new regression cases fail.
- After the fix: 33 Gemma4 processing cases pass, including all 8 new cases. One test requiring external image assets was excluded.
- Generic hash and parameter-scoping tests: 8 pass.
- Applicable pre-commit checks pass. Actionlint was skipped after its dependency download failed; this patch changes only Python files.

The Gemma4 runs used a local wrapper that redirects checkpoint loading to generated processor/config files and a minimal tokenizer. commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel] Integrate DeepSelect TopK for the DSA sparse indexer
commits.pr_body:
## What

Integrate [DeepSeek DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect) (MIT) — a high-performance TopK kernel library for DeepSeek Sparse Attention — into vLLM via CMake FetchContent, and make **every** decode top-k implementation on the DSA sparse indexer path explicitly selectable, with a measured auto heuristic on top.

- New optional extension `vllm._deepselect_C` (`cmake/external_projects/deepselect.cmake`), compiled only for sm_100a/sm_103a (nvcc >= 12.9); empty placeholder target elsewhere. Built against the PyTorch stable ABI (`STABLE_TORCH_LIBRARY`, `USE_SABI 3`, torch 2.10 target) — source is the `stable-abi` branch at `ZJY0516/DeepSelect` @ `c0e1f9cd` (the pybind11 → stable-ABI rework; plan is to move it upstream and switch the FetchContent repo back to deepseek-ai/DeepSelect). `DEEPSELECT_SRC_DIR` overrides the source for local builds.
- New `vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py`: the indexer's decode top-k stage. Hosts every backend entry point (DeepSelect, cooperative, persistent, per_row, FlashInfer ragged, torch reference) and `SparseIndexerTopk`, an `nn.Module` that resolves and runs one per step. `SparseAttnIndexer` just calls `SparseIndexerTopk()(...)`.
- New `KernelConfig.sparse_indexer_topk_backend` (`--sparse-indexer-topk-backend`): `auto` (default) / `deep_select` / `cooperative` / `persistent` / `per_row` / `flashinfer` / `torch`. Explicit values fail fast with the specific unmet constraint.
- Per-row `seq_lens` map directly onto DeepSelect's `end` parameter; output is written into the preallocated `topk_indices` buffer (CUDA-graph safe; the test below captures and replays every backend).


## Why not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for "DeepSelect" and "topk kernel sparse": no PR integrates DeepSelect. Related but different work: #56346 (sampled filtering inside persistent top-k), #48726 (a custom fused LiteTopk kernel), #55872 (deterministic FlashInfer top-k). This PR vendors DeepSeek's kernels unchanged and adds a shape-based dispatch, rather than modifying existing kernels.

## Performance (NVIDIA GB200, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUPTI timing, CUDA graph replay, cold L2)

Shapes from the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Lightning Indexer (`index_topk=512`; indexer "vocab" = KV context length). Scope of this PR is the sparse indexer only.

fp32 (vLLM's indexer logits), CUDA graph replay, vs the **pre-PR auto pick** for each shape (persistent for bs>64, cooperative for bs<=64), plus the other candidates:

| shape | DeepSelect | persistent (pre-PR default, bs>64) | cooperative (pre-PR default, bs<=64) | per_row | FlashInfer ragged | torch.topk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bs=256, kv=1M | **191us** (5.6 TB/s) | 616us | n/a (>64 rows) | 613us | 595us | 2878us |
| bs=64, kv=1M | **88us** | 303us | 132us | 206us | 206us | 905us |
| bs=8, kv=1M | 85us | 180us | **40us** (auto keeps cooperative) | 89us | 95us | 194us |

bf16 (DeepSelect's native dtype; vLLM's fp32 kernels don't apply), eager microbench: bs=256, kv=1M: **119us** (4.5 TB/s) vs FlashInfer 529us vs torch.topk 1855us.

## Tests

All in `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`:

- `test_deep_select_topk` / `test_deep_select_topk_preallocated_output` — wrapper correctness (fp32/bf16, variable per-row `end`, -1 fill, NaN-filled dirty tail proving the kernel never reads past `end`, preallocated strided output buffer).
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_topk_explicit_backends` — every explicit backend x next_n {1,4}: per-row length restriction, -1 fill, set/value equality vs torch.topk.
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_topk_short_seq_lens` — seq_len < next_n with spec decode: derived row ends clamp at 0 (matching the reference kernels' `max(0, ...)`); negative ends would be OOB for the ragged kernels.
- `test_sparse_indexer_topk_backend_resolution` — pins the auto chain (unchanged from main) and the fail-fast errors of every explicit backend.

Full file: 42/42 topk-related cases pass on GB200; `pre-commit run` on all touched files passes.

## Model eval

  - GSM8K flexible：0.9333
  - strict match：0.9325

## Notes / open questions

- Blackwell-only for now: DeepSelect upstream compiles sm_100a/sm_103a only.
- DeepSelect's sampling top-k (fp32, vocab 129280) also beats torch/FlashInfer at large batch — left for a follow-up, this PR is sparse-indexer only.
- AI assistance: this PR was implemented with AI assistance (Kimi Code); I have reviewed the changes and run the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Pooling] Support prompt embeddings in MRV2 decoder pooling
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

A regression bug fix between MRV1 and MRV2 for pooling decoder models (ie. `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`, etc),

MRV2's prompt-embedding state supports precomputed embeddings, but the pooling request path unconditionally asserted that `prompt_token_ids` was present. Decoder pooling requests that supplied `prompt_embeds` therefore crashed before inference, even though most pooling tasks do not need token IDs.

This PR makes the pooling-runner input optional and enforces the token-ID requirement only for tasks that declare `requires_token_ids`. Normal tokenized requests and token-ID-dependent pooling tasks retain the existing behavior.

## Reproducer

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import torch
from vllm import LLM

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B",
    runner="pooling",
    enable_prompt_embeds=True,
    max_model_len=64,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.15,
)
hidden_size = llm.llm_engine.model_config.get_hidden_size()
outputs = llm.embed(
    [
        {"prompt_embeds": torch.randn(4, hidden_size)},
        "ordinary token input",
    ]
)
print(
    "runner_v2",
    llm.llm_engine.vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner,
    "outputs",
    len(outputs),
    "embedding_dims",
    [len(output.outputs.embedding) for output in outputs],
)
PY
```

## Output on `main`

```text
assert new_req_data.prompt_token_ids is not None
AssertionError
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

## Output on this branch

```text
runner_v2 True outputs 2 embedding_dims [1024, 1024]
```

## Model accuracy and regression results

Direct token-ID versus equivalent precomputed-input-embedding comparisons:

| Decoder pooling model | Output width | Maximum absolute difference | Mean absolute difference | Cosine similarity |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` | 1024 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 1.0 |
| `BAAI/bge-multilingual-gemma2` | 3584 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 1.0000006 |
| `intfloat/e5-mistral-7b-instruct` | 4096 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 1.0 |

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_prompt_embeds_state.py -q
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Make streaming TTFT/E2E latency accounting consistent across endpoints
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`vllm/benchmarks/serve.py` derives TPOT from the end of the request:

```python
latency_minus_ttft = outputs[i].latency - outputs[i].ttft
tpot = latency_minus_ttft / (output_len - 1)
```

For that to mean "average inter-token latency", `latency - ttft` has to equal
`sum(itl)`. Today it does not, and it fails differently per endpoint, so E2EL
and TPOT are not comparable between an `openai` run and an `openai-chat` run.

Two independent causes:

**1. TTFT is read off a second clock call (`/v1/completions`).**

```python
timestamp = time.perf_counter()          # chunk arrival; seeds the ITL chain
if not first_chunk_received:
    first_chunk_received = True
    ttft = time.perf_counter() - st      # a different, later reading
    output.ttft = ttft
...
most_recent_timestamp = timestamp        # the earlier reading
```

TTFT is measured from one reading while the ITL chain continues from another,
so `latency - ttft` comes up short by the gap between the two calls.
`async_request_openai_chat_completions` and `async_request_openai_audio` already
do the right thing (`output.ttft = timestamp - st`), so this aligns completions
with its siblings rather than introducing a new convention.

**2. The trailing `usage` chunk extends E2E latency (chat and audio).**

`vllm bench serve` always sends `stream_options.include_usage`, so every stream
ends with a choice-less `usage` chunk after the last token. In chat and audio,
`most_recent_timestamp = timestamp` sits *outside* the `if choices:` branch, so
that trailer advances the end of the request; `output.latency` therefore runs
past the final token. `async_request_openai_completions` updates it *inside*
the branch and stops at the last token. `serve.py` assigns
`e2els.append(outputs[i].latency)` directly, so this lands in reported E2EL and
TPOT.

I fixed it in the direction that stops at the last token, because the
alternative — having completions also count the usage chunk — would break the
identity on *both* endpoints instead of fixing it: the usage gap appears in
`latency` but never in any `itl`. The loop already refuses to let the `[DONE]`
sentinel move the clock; the usage chunk is the same category of non-token
trailer.

`benchmarks/backend_request_func.py` carries the same two defects and is still
imported by `benchmark_prefix_caching.py` and
`benchmark_serving_structured_output.py`, so it gets the identical hunks (plus
the same one-line TTFT fix in `async_request_tgi`). Happy to split that file
into its own PR if you'd rather keep this one to `vllm/benchmarks/`.

### Magnitude — deliberately not overstated

This is a correctness and cross-endpoint-comparability fix, **not** a
performance claim. `chat_completion/serving.py` yields the usage chunk
immediately after the final content chunk in the same generator with no engine
await between, so in normal operation the error is tens of microseconds — I
measured ~24 µs on a 200 ms request, about 0.01%. The gap is not bounded by
anything, though: it is whatever separates two SSE writes, which on a saturated
client event loop is not guaranteed to stay small.

The lasting value is the test: `endpoint_request_func.py` currently has no test
coverage of its timing accounting at all, so nothing was stopping this from
drifting further.

## Not a duplicate

Per `AGENTS.md` I checked:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "endpoint_request_func"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "backend_request_func"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "usage chunk latency"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "benchmark ttft latency"
```

The only open PRs in this area are **#42661** and **#46652**, which both address
a *different* bug: servers batching multiple tokens into one SSE chunk, making
ITL per-chunk rather than per-token. Neither touches which clock reading TTFT
uses, nor where the request is considered to end. They are complementary — with
either merged, `sum(itl)` still spans the same decode window, so the identity
asserted here continues to hold.

#46652 also adds `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func.py`; this PR adds
`test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, so there is no filename collision, and
the two suites could be folded together later if that is preferred.

## Test Plan

New: `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py`, parametrized over
all three streaming request functions (completions, chat, audio). CPU-only — no
GPU, model, or socket; the request functions are driven against a fake session.

The exactness tests substitute a **scripted clock** that advances by a fixed
tick on every read. What a code path observes then depends only on how many
times it reads the clock, so a stray or misattributed read shows up as a whole
tick of drift instead of sub-microsecond jitter. That makes the assertions
exact and free of timing flakiness.

1. `test_decode_span_identity_is_exact` — `(latency - ttft) - sum(itl) == 0`.
2. `test_trailing_usage_chunk_does_not_extend_latency` — E2E latency stops at
   the final token.
3. `test_decode_span_identity_holds_with_real_clock` — same identity against the
   real clock with real inter-chunk gaps.
4. `test_usage_only_stream_is_not_reported_as_success` — a stream with no token
   chunk fails rather than reporting a zero-duration success. The residual differences out the same
   recorded timestamps, so jitter cancels and only float rounding remains; the
   1 µs bound is ample rather than tight.

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_audio_dataset.py -v   # sibling suite, same module
pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py \
    benchmarks/backend_request_func.py \
    tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py
```

## Test Result

On unpatched `main` (f4eccda), the new tests fail with the defects visible as
whole ticks of the scripted clock — negative for the extra TTFT read, positive
for the counted usage chunk:

```
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[completions]
  AssertionError: completions: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = -1.0
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[chat]
  AssertionError: chat: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = 1.0
FAILED test_decode_span_identity_is_exact[audio]
  AssertionError: audio: (latency - ttft) - sum(itl) = 1.0
8 failed, 1 passed
```

With the fix applied:

```
tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py 12 passed
tests/benchmarks/test_audio_dataset.py                 8 passed   (no regression)
(20 passed total)
```

Reverting only the two source files and re-running reproduces the 8 failures,
confirming the tests actually exercise the fix.

Independently, driving the unpatched request functions against a local SSE
server over a real socket, residual `(latency - ttft) - sum(itl)`:

| scenario | completions | chat |
|---|---|---|
| usage chunk emitted immediately (realistic) | −0.35 µs | +24.09 µs |
| usage chunk delayed 30 ms (mechanism probe) | −0.32 µs | **+31 473 µs** |

The probe isolates the mechanism: a 30 ms delay before the usage chunk moves
chat's residual by ~30 ms and leaves completions flat. After the fix, all four
cells are 0.00 µs.

`pre-commit` / `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean on all three files.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This changes only how the **benchmark client** measures latency
on the wire. No engine, scheduler, sampling, or serving path is touched, so
model outputs and accuracy are unaffected.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance. I have reviewed every changed
line, run the tests above myself, and can defend the change end-to-end.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][Perf][Quantization] Fix odd-row performance cliff in per-token-group quantization
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Avoid the odd-row performance cliff in per-token-group 8-bit quantization while preserving the existing launch policy for even row counts.

We identified this while investigating unexpectedly poor TPOT (time per output token) with Gemma 4 31B FP8 at TP8 on H100. The reproduction traced about 35 ms of extra time in a 13,359-token prefill forward pass to activation quantization, enough to erase the roughly 30 ms saved by FP8 GEMMs. At TP8, the down-projection input has width 2688: odd row counts launch 16-thread blocks and make quantization roughly 4× slower than the neighboring even case. The width-5376 inputs also take a roughly 2× slower path.

The current heuristic selects one group per block when the total group count is odd, launching only 16 threads. This change selects block geometry using the next even row count, then uses ceil-div and bounds checks for the actual groups. No tensors are padded or copied. All threads still participate in block and PDL synchronization, and the bounds check is compiled out for full blocks.

Quantization arithmetic and scale layouts are unchanged. The helper serves both FP8 and INT8, so both receive regression coverage. The separate packed kernel is unchanged.

### Related work

[#55330](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55330) takes a different approach: a register-resident kernel with fixed 256-thread launches for eligible inputs. This change retains the shared-memory kernel and its existing even-row policy, including support for FP32 inputs and group size 64. The approaches may be complementary, with this policy improving the shared-memory fallback.

## Performance

The H100 measurements below confirm the kernel improvement at the Gemma TP8 down-projection shape. End-to-end TP8 TPOT has not yet been remeasured with this patch.

Kernel latency in microseconds, measured with CUPTI and CUDA graphs. BF16 input, FP8 output, group size 128, column-major FP32 scales with UE8M0 rounding. Results are medians of three rounds of 30 samples; cold runs flush L2 outside the timed kernel.

| GPU | M × K | Hot before → after | Cold before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | 32767 × 128 | 41.76 → 10.45 | 41.86 → 12.48 |
| H100 | 32768 × 128 | 10.46 → 10.43 | 12.35 → 12.35 |
| H100 | 65537 × 128 | 81.18 → 41.82 | 81.22 → 41.86 |
| H100 | 13359 × 2688 | 339.63 → 81.46 | 339.63 → 83.38 |
| GB10 | 32767 × 128 | 49.23 → 20.93 | 85.98 → 89.10 |
| GB10 | 32768 × 128 | 20.80 → 20.82 | 87.14 → 86.62 |
| GB10 | 65537 × 128 | 108.24 → 67.47 | 146.27 → 145.66 |
| GB10 | 13359 × 2688 | 517.30 → 487.12 | 541.51 → 516.96 |

**H100:** The final production-source comparison covers 18 shapes, with geometric-mean latency reductions of 39.5% hot and 38.0% cold. An earlier 259-shape policy prototype also covered the broader matrix: all 112 odd shapes were within 2.9% hot and 4.2% cold of the next-even control. That prototype always enabled the guard for odd rows; the final patch omits it when no tail exists.

**GB10:** Across 182 general shapes, the geometric-mean latency reduction is 6.7% hot and 0.2% cold. Even-row performance remains essentially unchanged. Across 91 odd/next-even pairs, geometric-mean latency differs by less than 0.4%.

Clocks were not locked on either GPU. The H100 and GB10 aggregate matrices differ, so their averages are not a direct GPU comparison. H200, B200, B300, and ROCm were not tested.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing FP8 and INT8 tests with empty inputs, odd tails, FP16/BF16/FP32 inputs, group sizes 64/128, and supported scale layouts.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_per_token_group_quant_fp8 \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_per_token_group_quant_int8

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/fp8/per_token_group_quant.cu \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py
```

## Test Result

- Isolated production-source tests: **678 passed** on both H100 and GB10.
- GB10 Compute Sanitizer memcheck and synccheck: **zero errors**.
- GB10 validation reports **678 passed** with the rebuilt extension. Its command ledger names `test_utils.py` rather than the test file above; the recorded command needs reconciliation.
- Final production-source benchmarks produced byte-identical quantized outputs and identical scales against baseline on all **18 H100 shapes** and **194 GB10 shapes**.
- Repository hooks passed.
- GB10 Gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block loaded and generated the expected response to a deterministic text prompt through the modified quantizer. This was a serving smoke test; a broader model accuracy evaluation has not been run.

commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Share the replicated HiSparse MLA host cache across local TP ranks using one mmap-backed pool. TP rank 0 writes the shared pool; peers wait on its IPC events before reading it. Other executor and parallel layouts retain private pools.

This reopens #52760 against `main`. The original PR was automatically closed when [3/N] (#53781) merged and its base branch, `feat/hisparse-mla-decode-main`, was deleted.

I am not the original author of this work; I reopened the existing PR so it can continue through review. Credit goes to **Chao Lei (@LCAIZJ)**, the original PR author, and **Matthew Bonanni (@MatthewBonanni)** for their implementation and follow-up work. The original commit authorship, co-author credits, and sign-offs are preserved, including my previous follow-up fixes.

The 11 original shared-host-cache commits rebased cleanly onto `main` with unchanged patches. The preceding metrics commit is already covered by merged #56061. A follow-up simplifies shared-region initialization as described below.

## Implementation

- Resolve shared/private host-pool mode and the physical host-block stride in the cache planner and propagate them through `KVCacheConfig`.
- Check physical host RAM in the mmap creator only and populate the shared backing once.
- Reuse `SharedOffloadRegion`'s existing barrier with the TP CPU group instead of introducing file locks. The creator populates before the barrier; the file is unlinked after all workers have mapped it, protecting against backing-file leaks after SIGKILL.
- Keep the ordinary offload population path close to `main`. The shared-region diff is reduced from 164 changed lines to 85.
- Preserve initialization rollback and cleanup of every successful CUDA host registration. Registration boundaries remain aligned with transfer geometry.
- Extend the existing multiprocess test to cover replicated-slot visibility, creator-only population, and cleanup after SIGKILL; remove the redundant standalone sharing test.
- Correct the documentation to describe the single TP writer and remove the stale claim that `num_gpu_blocks_override` overrides host capacity.

## Duplicate-work check

This replaces closed #52760, which itself replaced closed #51324. Checked both PR discussions, open PRs referencing either number, and open HiSparse/shared-host-cache work before opening this replacement; no open PR carrying the same change was found.

## Validation

- `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_kv_cache_allocation_scope.py -q` — 4 passed. Fixed the outdated zero-argument `HiSparseHostPool` mock to accept the two config arguments introduced by this PR.

All 243 tests in the related suites therefore passed with the required GPU visibility.
- Local TP=2 CUDA smoke test through real vLLM distributed groups and `allocate_hisparse_host_pools`: all four cases passed (single/split registration, each across two allocation/cleanup cycles). Verified shared inode, early unlink, rank-0 GPU-to-host writes, IPC-event waits, exact host-to-GPU round trips on both ranks, and registration cleanup. commits.pr_title: [PCP][DCP] Enable PCP+DCP on sparse-MLA models
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Enable DCP to run alongside PCP on sparse-MLA models, so a deployment can shard the KV cache for decode and still split prefill query work across ranks.

This change:

- gives the sparse indexer a DCP-gathered prefill path: this rank's KV shard is all-gathered across the DCP group
- gives the FlashMLA-sparse backend the matching prefill path, with a rank-major gathered KV workspace and a PCP-invariant chunk plan every rank derives identically without communicating;
- replicates prefills too short to fill all `2*PCP` chunks when DCP is on, which keeps the per-region row count identical on every rank — the invariant the gathered layout rests on;
- adds a MoE all-reduce fast path for steps whose rows are all PCP-replicated, replacing an unconditional all-gather + reduce-scatter that duplicated every decode row `PCP` times;
- relaxes the PCP CUDA graph restriction for PCP+DCP to everything up to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, keeping only `FULL` over mixed batches rejected;

fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53573
Additionally
- fixes a pre-existing kernel/reference divergence: the top-k index kernel applied the block-table bound to prefill-workspace rows, while `_triton_convert_reference_impl` has always specified that only `-1` is invalid there. The existing test missed it because `token_indices[6, 150:160]` is an empty slice on a 128-column tensor;

## Test Plan

- NVIDIA GB200 x4
- GLM-5.3, NVFP4 weights
- TP=1, PCP=4, DCP=4

## Purpose

Elastic EP scaling sometimes hangs during a scale up/down on ROCm. This was seen from time to time in CI, e.g. [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12870/list?sid=01a08fb2-f7cc-4c10-b517-929727fc69e1&tab=output).

This was root-caused via RCCL logs: during elastic-EP prepare the standby/joining groups are built while the engine is still serving, so a new communicator warm-up (which does an all-reduce) might run concurrently with forward-pass collectives on the existing communicators, causing a race and potentially a deadlock if different collectives are enqueued in different order on different ranks.

Fix: On ROCm, defer the warm-up for standby/joining groups and run it at commit, when the scheduler is paused. Per @itayalroy it does not appear that CUDA runs into this deadlock, possibly because the concurrent collectives can issue simultaneously rather than serially (it does not appear that NCCL itself provides better ordering guarantees, see [here](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/574#issuecomment-927600504)).

Supersedes the draft #53010, which restricts the deferral to ROCm + cudagraph and does not cover all cases (including eager) in which the hangs occur.

## Test Plan
```
pytest -s tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py
```
This is run as part of the `Elastic EP Scaling` test group on main and AMD CI.


## Test Result
On 4x MI300X:
- `test_elastic_ep.py`: 2 failed (`enforce_eager_light`, `enforce_eager_heavy`)
  before, 5 passed after (run twice). GSM8K accuracy across scaling unchanged.

The `Elastic EP Scaling` test groups on AMD CI now reliably pass, and there are no new regressions.

commits.pr_title: [watermarking] Dual-key gumbel-max watermarking for speculative decoding support
commits.pr_body:
### Purpose
Text watermarking in vLLM (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54053) currently is not compatible with speculative decoding. This PR proposes multiple changes to resolve this:

- `"allow_target_only_watermarking": true` allows the use of speculative decoding with watermarking, but will not watermark accepted draft tokens: this will dilute the watermarking signal in proportion to the share of output tokens that are accepted drafts
- `dual_key_gumbel` algorithm is a variation of the Gumbel-max algorithm, where we use different keys to watermark our generations: this allows for watermarking of draft tokens, and also for improved diversity of outputs when using watermarking

Dual-key watermarking allows to support speculative decoding by using algorithm 6 of [SynthID-Text's supplementary material](https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-024-08025-4/MediaObjects/41586_2024_8025_MOESM1_ESM.pdf). To watermark the draft model's generations, without inducing a loss in acceptance rate (see algorithm 5):

```
Given distinct watermarking keys k^T and k^D, a target model p, a draft model q, a watermarked target model p_wm(.;k^T) and draft model q_wm(.;k^D)

1. We sample draft tokens from q_wm
2. We calculate target logits for drafts using p
3. We accept tokens with probability r < min(1, q(x) / p(x))
4. If rejected, we sample from residual(p, q)(.;k^T)
5. If all tokens are accepted, we sample our bonus token from p_wm
```

Note how:
- all draft tokens are watermarked by k^D
- all target tokens are watermarked by k^T (residual, and bonus)
- acceptance rate uses unwatermarked distributions, and is identical to acceptance rate without watermarking

For justification of using distinct keys to preserve non-distortion, see section K.13 of [SynthID-Text's supplementary material](https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-024-08025-4/MediaObjects/41586_2024_8025_MOESM1_ESM.pdf).

### Test Plan
Measuring impact, using standard models and methods, on:
- inference performance (in particular the acceptance rate)
- detectability of watermark

### Test Result
Results for commit `97a264006f3d7ed9999fbd9b93319b780ac0631d` on 1x H100 per arm.

GSM8K, 300 five-shot prompts, temperature 1.0, maximum 1,024 output tokens, and Qwen3.5 MTP with three probabilistically sampled draft tokens.

#### Inference performance

| Model | Disabled output tokens | Dual-key output tokens | Disabled tok/s | Dual-key tok/s | Delta throughput |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-2B | 59,769 | 72,141 | 7,366.0 | 8,254.0 | +12.1% |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 102,555 | 101,330 | 1,268.0 | 1,215.9 | -4.1% |

The generated length distributions differ, especially for the 2B model, so these are end-to-end workload measurements rather than an isolated measure of watermarking overhead.

#### Speculative decoding

| Model | Watermark | Draft acceptance rate | Mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-2B | Disabled | 69.6% | 3.09 |
| Qwen3.5-2B | Dual-key Gumbel | 79.9% | 3.40 |
| Qwen3.5-27B | Disabled | 81.1% | 3.43 |
| Qwen3.5-27B | Dual-key Gumbel | 80.9% | 3.43 |

Per-request speculative metrics were only populated for requests that performed speculative steps. The table aggregates the accepted and drafted token counts from those records.

#### Quality

| Model | Watermark | Accuracy | Mean completion length | Median completion length | Repeated 4-token context rate (micro) | Reached 1,024-token cap |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-2B | Disabled | 25.7% | 199.2 | 128.0 | 20.48% | 14/300 (4.7%) |
| Qwen3.5-2B | Dual-key Gumbel | 25.0% | 240.5 | 123.5 | 41.97% | 33/300 (11.0%) |
| Qwen3.5-27B | Disabled | 64.0% | 341.9 | 165.0 | 20.44% | 59/300 (19.7%) |
| Qwen3.5-27B | Dual-key Gumbel | 73.0% | 337.8 | 164.5 | 19.56% | 53/300 (17.7%) |

These are single stochastic runs, so accuracy differences should not be interpreted as causal.

#### Detectability

Detection uses the exact completion token IDs, both derived keys, context deduplication, and a threshold of p ≤ 0.01.

| Model | No-watermark positives | Dual-key positives | Median dual-key p-value | Mean dual-key scored tokens |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-2B | 3/300 (1.0%) | 226/300 (75.3%) | 0.000145 | 139.5 |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 3/300 (1.0%) | 69/300 (23.0%) | 0.113773 | 271.7 |

Detection improves with completion length:

| Model | <64 tokens | 64-127 | 128-255 | 256-511 | ≥512 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-2B | 40.5% | 70.9% | 80.6% | 100.0% | 100.0% |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 0.0% | 4.6% | 8.5% | 50.0% | 64.7% |

Poor detectability on the 27B generations are due to low entropy, which reduces the amount of signal our watermarking bias can embed:

| Model | Perplexity | Sampled tokens with p ≥ 0.99 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-2B | 2.25 | 36.1% |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 1.19 | 72.7% |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepGEMM FP8 warmup coverage
commits.pr_body:
# [Bugfix] Fix DeepGEMM FP8 warmup coverage

DeepGEMM warmup missed compressed-tensors and ModelOpt block-FP8 layers, including block-FP8 ParallelLMHead layers. It also excluded supported weight shapes whose output dimension N is divisible by 64 but not 128. The missed compressed-tensors layers caused kernels to JIT compile during requests in the Gemma run below, producing 10–20 second stalls.

The DeepGEMM linear kernel now registers a warmup provider during weight loading. Warmup uses that provider to find eligible layers and weights. This also covers the FlashInfer dynamic fallback, skips BMM layers, and shares scale lookup through `FP8BlockParams.block_scale`.

## Related work

The duplicate check recorded on 2026-09-11 found:

- #50617 adds ModelOpt-specific lookup. This PR overlaps that fix but replaces attribute probing with kernel registration, also covering compressed-tensors, `ParallelLMHead`, and supported non-128-aligned shapes.
- #49930 addresses BMM/einsum warmup, which this change excludes.
- #41851 skips warmup when DeepGEMM is unavailable.

## Validation

Commands and results from the recorded runs:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k fp8_block -v
```

- Warmup tests: 6 passed on CPU and 6 on H100. Covers both scale names, supported shapes, skipped layers, and provider registration.
- Compressed-tensors: `[auto]` passed; `[marlin]` failed with `cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion` in `marlin_utils_fp8.py`. The recorded cause was a toolchain mismatch: driver 580 supports CUDA 13.0; extensions used 13.3.
- Ruff check and format: clean on all four changed files.

### Serving and model output

Tested `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block` on one H100 80GB with CUDA 13.3, vendored DeepGEMM, and a fresh `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` per run.

| Configuration | Layers warmed | JIT cache entries after load |
| --- | --- | --- |
| This PR, `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=relax` | 240 / 240 | 72 |
| This PR, `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip` | 0 | 51 |
| Main (`3735c2d5f`), `relax` | 0 | 51 |

Warmup took 84 seconds. With warmup skipped, a sweep of 463 prompt sizes found three request-time compilation stalls:

| Prompt tokens | First request | Repeat request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 517 | 12.5 s | 0.05 s |
| 641 | 9.7 s | 0.05 s |
| 785 | 20.0 s | 0.07 s |

All 11 kernels compiled by these requests were present in this PR's warmup cache and absent from main's.

commits.pr_title: [4/N] Expose HiSparse cache metrics via KV connector stats
commits.pr_body:
Alternative to #53782, reporting the same HiSparse hot-buffer stats through the existing `KVConnectorStats` pipeline instead of adding a new `finish_step` connector hook.

## What stays identical

- Kernel counters (`atomicAdd` in the CUDA kernels) and the swap-ordering changes in `runtime.py` are unchanged from the original PR.
- Same 2000-step async sampling interval with a CUDA event for D2H ordering.
- Same three Prometheus counters: `vllm:hisparse_hits`, `vllm:hisparse_lookups`, `vllm:hisparse_l3_lookups`.

## What changes

Instead of a new `finish_step` hook on `KVConnectorBase` (plus edits to scheduler, outputs, aggregator, loggers, and `stats.py`), the worker now exposes the snapshots through the existing hook:

```python
def get_kv_connector_stats(self) -> Optional[HiSparseKVConnectorStats]:
    ...
```

and the connector wires it into the standard pipeline:

```
worker.get_kv_connector_stats()          # HiSparseKVConnectorStats (list of snapshot deltas)
  -> scheduler picks it up in SchedulerStats
  -> build_kv_connector_stats()          # HiSparseKVConnectorStats.from_proxy_stats
  -> HiSparsePromMetrics.observe()       # vllm:hisparse_* counters
```

This is the same contract NIXL, the offloading connector, and mooncake already follow — transfer/cache telemetry goes through `KVConnectorStats` and the connector's `build_prom_metrics`, with zero core plumbing. HiSparse's hot-buffer residency counters are connector telemetry, so they fit the same slot the offloading connector uses for its allocation-failure/lookup-delay stats.

Net effect: the diff drops from 16 files to 9 and avoids changes to `base.py`, `model_runner.py`, `outputs.py`, scheduler, loggers, and core `stats.py`.

Also picks up two small cleanups over the original:

- Stats emission is gated on the connector being configured (the connector owns its stats, rather than gating on `attention_config` in the model runner).
- The sampling interval advances even on no-forward steps, so long prefill stretches don't stretch the sampling cadence.

Because the stats flow through `KVConnectorStats`, CLI logging comes for free:

```
INFO ... Cumulative HiSparse stats: hits=12 lookups=4 l3_lookups=64
```

## Validation

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py::test_hisparse_worker_get_kv_connector_stats_reads_completed_snapshot -q
6 passed

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py
All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, and mypy.
```

Model evaluation is not applicable because this change only reports telemetry and does not affect model outputs.

Duplicate check: this remains the `KVConnectorStats`-based alternative to #53782; searches for open PRs mentioning #56061 and HiSparse metrics found no duplicate of this implementation.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped audit CI and prepare the follow-up cleanup. Human review and ownership remain with the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Add DSv4.1 auto-label rules and narrow DSv4
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 had no label of its own, and the existing `DSv4` patterns were
claiming all of its traffic.

`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` is a distinct architecture from `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`:
its own model tree (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/`), its own `tokenizer_mode`
(`deepseek_v41`), and its own tokenizer, parser, reasoning parser, tool parser and
config class. It adds `common/engram.py`, `nvidia/model_state.py`,
`common/ops/indexer_k_store.py` and `common/ops/query_quant.py`, and carries none
of V4's `mtp.py`, `cpu/`, `xpu/`, `fi_moe.py` or `common/vision.py`.

Two concrete defects follow from having no separate label:

1. **`DSv4` captures every V4.1 title.** Nothing bounded the version after `v4`,
   so `deepseek[-\s]?v4` matched `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` and `\bDSv4\b` matched
   `DSv4.1`. #56228, a pure V4.1 PR, is labeled `DSv4`.
2. **The issue labeler missed space-separated titles.** Its `DSv4` matcher was the
   substring `deepseek-v4` plus the keyword `DSv4`, while mergify allowed
   `[-\s]?`. #56297 ("DeepSeek V4.1 rejects Responses API text content types") got
   `deepseek` and nothing else. This is a pre-existing V4 gap, not a V4.1 one.

## Changes

- `.github/mergify.yml`: add `label-dsv41`; bound `label-dsv4`'s title pattern
  with `(?![._]?1)`.
- `.github/workflows/issue_autolabel.yml`: add a `"DSv4.1"` entry; convert `DSv4`
  from substring matching to the same bounded regex so both labelers agree.

The 4.1 sources spell the model three ways — `deepseek_v4_1` (models),
`deepseek_v41` (most), `deepseekv41` (tool parsers) — so the file conditions cover
all three.

**Flash and Pro share one label per generation.** They are the same code path in
vLLM: one arch string, one config class, no variant branching anywhere in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/`, and the V4-Flash and V4-Pro eval configs are identical
but for the model name and load timeout. No file condition could distinguish them,
so a per-variant label would only ever be title-routable.

## Prerequisite

The `DSv4.1` label must exist before this merges; a rule naming a nonexistent
label does not create it.

## Not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --state open --search "dsv4.1 label"` — no results.
- `gh pr list --state open --search "mergify label automation"` — no results
  touching label config.
- `gh issue view 56217 --comments` (the V4.1 kernel tracking issue) — no labeling
  work claimed.

No open PR modifies `.github/mergify.yml` or the issue labeler.

## Testing

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files .github/mergify.yml .github/workflows/issue_autolabel.yml
.venv/bin/python tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py
```

Both pass, including `actionlint` and `check-label-rules`. I verified
`check-label-rules` is not passing vacuously: injecting a deliberately dead glob
makes it fail and name `label-dsv41`.

Beyond the hooks, I validated out of tree against 25 real V4/V4.1 titles taken
from this repo's history, in both engines the two labelers use — Python `re` for
mergify and JS `RegExp` for the workflow — and by executing the workflow's own
`labelConfig` and matching functions with stubbed `core`/`github`/`context`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 25 real titles, Python | 25/25 |
| 25 real titles, JS | 25/25 |
| Workflow's real matching logic | all pass |
| File conditions vs tree | 44/44 V4.1 files, no overmatch, no bleed onto `DSv4` |
| `DSv4` conditions still live | 51 files |
| No title receives both labels | confirmed |
| Noisy body does not leak model labels | confirmed; title-only design holds |

Representative outcomes:

| Title | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[Bug]: DeepSeek V4.1 rejects Responses API text content types` (#56297) | `deepseek` | `deepseek`, `DSv4.1` |
| `[Model] Support DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` | `deepseek`, `DSv4` | `deepseek`, `DSv4.1` |
| `[Bugfix][DSv4] Keep indexer scoring in breakable graphs` | `deepseek`, `DSv4` | unchanged |
| `[Model] Support DeepSeek-V4-Pro` | `deepseek`, `DSv4` | unchanged |

Happy to commit the title-regex cases as a test if reviewers want a permanent
guard; there is no existing suite covering `.github/` matcher behavior, and
`check-label-rules` covers only the file conditions.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This touches CI labeling configuration only — no engine, kernel,
model or serving code, so there is no effect on output or accuracy.

## Follow-up

Once the label exists, ~14 open V4.1 PRs and 2 issues need backfilling, and
#56228's `DSv4` should be corrected to `DSv4.1`.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the labeling gap, write these
rules and run the validation above. I have reviewed every changed line, confirmed
the architectural distinction the change rests on, and run the test commands
listed.
